renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: bgc_genome_track
  title: Cluster regions on the contigs
  description: |-
    Each interval is a predicted biosynthetic gene cluster placed on its contig, with its height giving the region length in kilobases and its colour the product class. It answers where on the assembly the clusters sit and which kinds they are.
    How to read: several clusters on one contig suggest a biosynthetic locus, and a cluster covering a whole short contig is probably truncated by the contig edge. Compare the classes: a contig that carries several different ones is a promising place to look first.
    Note: callers disagree on region boundaries by design, so the same locus can appear as differently sized intervals. No cut-off on region length is published, so no line is drawn.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  kind: genome_view
  config:
    score_title: Region length (kb)
  roles:
    chr: contig
    pos: start
    score: length_kb
    feature: region_id
    end: end
    category: product_class

- component: advanced_viz
  id: bgc_region_arrows
  title: Clusters as lanes per contig
  description: |-
    Each arrow is a predicted cluster drawn along its contig, one lane per contig and coloured by product class. It answers how clusters are arranged along a contig.
    How to read: arrows packed next to each other mark a dense biosynthetic locus, and different colours in one lane mean a contig with several kinds of cluster. Overlapping arrows on a locus are usually the same cluster called by different tools.
    Note: comBGC does not report a strand, so arrows carry no direction.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  kind: gene_arrow_track
  roles:
    contig: contig
    feature_id: region_id
    start: start
    end: end
    strand: strand
    class: product_class
    label: product_class

- component: advanced_viz
  id: bgc_region_coverage
  title: Region length along the contigs
  description: |-
    Each bar is a predicted cluster on a contig, as tall as the region is long in kilobases and coloured by product class, with samples shown separately. It answers how long the predicted clusters are and where they fall.
    How to read: very short regions sitting at the start of a contig are often fragments cut by the contig edge, while long ones are more likely to be full clusters. Use it where the genome tracks are unavailable.
    Note: no cut-off on region length is published, so no line is drawn.
  kind: coverage_track
  roles:
    chromosome: contig
    position: start
    value: length_kb
    end: end
    sample: sample
    category: product_class

- component: card
  id: region_length
  title: Typical cluster length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median region length in kilobases, and the bars rank the product classes by their own median. It answers how long clusters are and which classes are the longest.
    How to read: the minimum and maximum show how much lengths vary, which is wide because regions run from a few genes to whole megacomplexes. Regions cut by a contig edge pull the median down.
  column: length_kb
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: product_class
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: median length (kb), by product class

- component: card
  id: region_count
  title: Predicted clusters
  description: |-
    The hero number is the number of predicted clusters, the bars rank the product classes by how many clusters each has, and the line below gives the typical and largest gene count. It answers which kinds of cluster dominate.
    How to read: a leading class is the main biosynthetic potential of the sample. Classes named Unknown or with a generic label come from callers that do not type every region.
  column: cds_count
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: product_class
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: clusters, by product class

- component: table
  title: Cluster coordinates
  description: |-
    One row per predicted cluster with its contig, interval, product class and length. Selecting rows filters the tab to that contig.
    How to read: sort by length to find the largest clusters.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: contig

- component: advanced_viz
  id: bgc_hierarchy
  title: Callers and product classes
  description: |-
    Each arc is a group of predicted clusters: the inner ring is the prediction tool and the outer ring the product class, sized by the number of clusters and coloured by tool. It answers which caller contributes which kinds of cluster.
    How to read: a wide arc under one caller only means that caller alone detects the class. Class names are not shared between callers, so the same kind of cluster can appear under different names. Click an arc to zoom in on it.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  kind: sunburst
  config:
    colour_by_rank: tool
  roles:
    ranks:
    - tool
    - product_class
    abundance: regions

- component: figure
  id: regions_per_sample
  title: Clusters per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is the number of predicted clusters in one sample, split by product class. It answers how rich each sample is in biosynthetic gene clusters and of which kinds.
    How to read: a tall bar with several classes means a sample with diverse potential. Differences between samples may follow assembly size and caller sensitivity as much as biology, so compare with care.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: regions
    color: product_class
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      regions: Predicted clusters
      product_class: Product class

- component: card
  id: cluster_count
  title: Predicted clusters
  description: |-
    The hero number is the number of predicted clusters, the bars rank the product classes by how many clusters each has, and the line below gives the number of distinct classes. It answers how many clusters were found and which kinds lead.
    How to read: a leading class is the main biosynthetic potential. Many distinct classes with a few clusters each mean a diverse but shallow profile.
  column: product_class
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: product_class
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: clusters, by product class
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: contigs_with_clusters
  title: Contigs with clusters
  description: |-
    The hero number is the number of distinct contigs holding at least one predicted cluster, the bars rank the callers by how many contigs each reports, and the line below gives the cluster count. It answers how widely clusters are spread over the assembly.
    How to read: more clusters than contigs means several clusters share a contig. A caller reporting far fewer contigs than the others is more conservative.
  column: contig
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: tool
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: contigs, by prediction tool

- component: card
  id: cluster_length
  title: Typical cluster length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median cluster length in base pairs, and the bars rank the callers by their own median. It answers how long the predicted regions are and whether callers draw them alike.
    How to read: callers disagree on region boundaries by design, so a systematically longer median for one tool reflects how it sets edges. Lengths span orders of magnitude, so read the minimum and maximum beside the median.
  column: length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: tool
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: median length (bp), by prediction tool

- component: card
  id: cds_per_cluster
  title: Genes per cluster
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average number of coding sequences in a predicted cluster, and the histogram shows how the counts are distributed. It answers how large clusters are in genes.
    How to read: a pile of single-gene clusters means short or truncated regions. A long tail marks large, multi-gene biosynthetic clusters.
  column: cds_count
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distribution of gene counts

- component: table
  title: Predicted clusters
  description: |-
    One row per predicted cluster with its caller, product class, coordinates, gene count and domain richness. Selecting rows filters the tab to that contig.
    How to read: sort by gene count or domain richness to find the most complex clusters.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: contig

- component: advanced_viz
  id: bgc_upset
  title: Caller concordance
  description: |-
    Each bar is the number of contigs predicted to hold a cluster by one combination of callers, and the dots below show which callers. It answers which callers agree on a contig and which find clusters alone.
    How to read: tall bars of one caller alone mean clusters only that caller finds, and bars shared by all callers mark the most reliable calls. Little overlap is normal because callers use different methods.
    Note: agreement is scored on the contig, because callers set region boundaries differently and a coordinate join would report no overlap.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/funcscan/master/docs/output.md
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    color_intersections_by: set

- component: table
  title: Callers per contig
  description: |-
    One row per contig with a 0 or 1 for each caller that predicted a cluster on it.
    How to read: filter on a caller to list the contigs it alone reports.
